title: Continuous KV cache quantization calibration and regression harness (INT8/FP8)
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: build and validate a continuous calibration + regression harness for KV-cache quantization profiles targeting INT8 and FP8 modes. The harness must enable repeatable offline sweeps, nightly incremental calibration on drifting traffic, and deterministic regression checks against a golden prompt set. This ticket scopes: the experiment harness, calibration workflows, validation metrics, and proposed routing/fallback policies for production rollout.

Background: previous KV quantization experiments showed promising cost/throughput wins but inconsistent quality on long-context sequences when naive symmetric quantization was used. This work focuses on two operational goals: (1) robust calibration that minimizes brittle edge-case failures caused by per-batch activation outliers and cross-request KV reuse, and (2) an automated regression gate that prevents quality regressions from being promoted to Dedicated/Hosted pools.

Scope and approach:
- Calibration workflows: implement two pipelines and compare results: 
  * Offline batch calibration: collect representative KV activations from 5M tokens sampled across customers and inference modes, compute per-layer asymmetric scales using a percentile-based clipping (default percentile=99.95), and emit quantization profiles.
  * Online micro-calibration: light-weight on-device observer that refines layer scales using exponential moving averages (EMA alpha=0.01) sampled from recent requests; designed to be bounded and reversible.
- Per-layer asymmetric scales and bias compensation: prefer asymmetric int8 with per-channel scales for KV query/key/value tensors, plus a small bias correction term learned from calibration set to reduce logit shift. For fp8 profiles we evaluate scaled-fp8 (E4M3 and E5M2 variants) with profile-specific mantissa choices.
- Validation datasets: split golden prompt corpus into calibration/validation/test (60/20/20). Golden set includes: retrieval-augmented prompts, long-context conversational continuations (up to 16k tokens), and code generation examples.
- Metrics: automated checks include token-level perplexity delta, average logit cosine similarity (LCS), top-1/top-5 accuracy, MRR for ranking tasks, and human-eval pass rate (golden QA). We also track QPS and P95 latency on synthetic load. Thresholds: reject if MRR drops >1.5% absolute or LCS < 0.985 on validation set.
- Latency/quality trade-offs: instrument microbench to capture per-token latency, KV memory consumption, and end-to-end p95. Expectation from initial pilots: INT8 reduces KV memory by ~2.1x and gives ~12-20% lower p95 vs fp32; FP8 gives ~1.5x memory reduction with <8% p95 improvement but better fidelity on long-context generation.

Preliminary results (summary of runs 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-20):
- INT8 asymmetric + bias-comp yielded avg MRR delta -1.1% and LCS 0.988 on the 2k-context split; p95 reduced by 18% on A100 pools.
- FP8 (E4M3) on same model: MRR delta -0.3%, LCS 0.996; p95 reduced by 9%.
- Mixed-profile strategy (use FP8 for context>4k, INT8 for <=4k) showed combined benefits: weighted p95 improvement ~13% and MRR delta -0.6%.
- Notable failure mode: edge-case sequences with repeated long-span attention (document summarization with heavy repetition) produced cascading KV rounding error in INT8 unless clipping percentile tuned to 99.995.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness implemented and integrated into CI with nightly sweep job that produces artifacted quant profiles and a regression report.
- Repro script documented and runnable by infra team (see reproduction steps below).
- If mixed-profile routing adopted, implement a config knob in runtime to route by context-length and model variant.
- No regression on golden test set beyond thresholds defined above.

Repro steps (local dev):
1) Checkout runtime branch: git checkout feat/kv-quant-harness && git pull origin.
2) Prepare calibration corpus: scripts/collect_kv_activations.sh --sample 500000 --out /tmp/kv_calib.npz.
3) Run offline calibrator: cargo run --bin kv_calibrator -- --input /tmp/kv_calib.npz --profile out/kv_profile_int8.json --percentile 99.95.
4) Run regression harness: python tools/quant_regress.py --profile out/kv_profile_int8.json --model model_dir/ --golden tests/golden_prompts.json --metrics out/regress-results.json.

Rollout proposal and fallback policy:
- Canary: deploy profile to 5% of requests in Dedicated, monitor regression metrics + user errors for 48h.
- If MRR delta within threshold but p95 regresses >12% relative to baseline, route to an INT8-safe fallback (INT8 if currently FP8, or fp32 if INT8 failing).
- After 7 days of stable canary, gradual increase to 50% then 100% for capacity-limited customers.

Next steps:
- Finish integrating the online micro-calibration observer into runtime (blocked by ENG-63413).
- Add QA automations to convert regression output into a console grafana panel and alert (ENG-63414).
- Run a 7-day A/B on two medium-sized customers and collect production drift numbers.

Notes and trade-offs:
- We accept slightly higher memory overhead for FP8 profiles to preserve fidelity on long contexts at the cost of smaller latency gains.
- INT8 is attractive for cost-driven tiers; we need guardrails (clipping percentiles, bias-comp) to avoid cascading KV errors.
- The harness must be deterministic and archive raw activations and seed values for future investigations.
